findings.title: Wallet answer snapshots discard valid prototype getters
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Resolve the regression in the supported public WalletMatch contract before release.
findings.reproduction: Call askWallet with a class whose prototype getters return matched:true and path:'m'. Also use an own matched:true field with path provided by a prototype getter.
findings.expected: Accept both structurally valid WalletMatch objects and retain their declared result fields, reading each once.
findings.observed: The class is refused as malformed; the second answer is accepted with its path silently omitted. Two independent probe cases fail.
findings.impact: Supported library hosts can lose a successful wallet match or its evidence after the remediation's object-spread snapshot. Native CLI answers are ordinary own-property objects and were not shown to fail. No forged wallet or secret disclosure is demonstrated.
findings.recommendedFix: Snapshot the declared WalletMatch fields by reading each once; preserve generic host result fields according to their contract. Do not assume supported fields are enumerable own properties.
findings.requiredVerification: Class/prototype and non-enumerable result fields must work; keep changing-getter snapshot controls and rejection of malformed matched values.

findings.title: Listed-code results still return after cancellation during fingerprinting
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited cancellation or best-effort cleanup gap; no direct secret compromise shown.
findings.reproduction: Read '2027 10 2? 2027 10 24 2027 10 24 2027 10 377' as indexes/Seedshift and list candidates for 23-09-2026. Its fingerprint callback aborts the signal with Error('public list stop') and returns '00000000'.
findings.expected: Under the strengthened no-late-publication promise, reject with the same abort reason before returning the list.
findings.observed: ListWay.run returns kind:'list' while the signal is already aborted. The shared guard runs inside searched, before the later fingerprint awaits.
findings.impact: A stopped library/browser recovery can publish a late candidate list. The original wallet-based AUD-015 reproductions now pass; this is another continuation of the same cancellation root cause. No wrong wallet or native secret leak is shown.
findings.recommendedFix: Call the existing shared assertStillRunning after the awaited fingerprint and before list publication/final return; do not add a separate cancellation policy.
findings.requiredVerification: Abort inside an asynchronous fingerprint must reject with its reason, while ordinary list and wallet searches continue to work.

findings.title: Throwing transport mappers leave partially populated arrays unwiped
findings.releaseBlockingReason: Limited cancellation or best-effort cleanup gap; no direct secret compromise shown.
findings.reproduction: Replace the last minimal Bytewords pair of a published UR share with 'zz', or its last full Byteword with 'zzzz'. Capture allocations by applying the original Uint8Array.from with a capturing Uint8Array subclass as its constructor.
findings.expected: Refuse the unknown token and wipe internally owned decoded bytes, including partial allocations created before a mapper throws.
findings.observed: Both readers refuse correctly, but each captured partial allocation still contains nonzero decoded share bytes. The mapper throws before from returns an array to the caller's cleanup wrapper.
findings.impact: The ordinary successful-read and invalid-metadata buffers are now wiped; malformed-token failures retain an internal decoded prefix. This is a best-effort secret-lifecycle gap, not proof of heap-wide erasure failure or attacker access to process memory. Caller-owned valid output must stay usable.
findings.recommendedFix: Use an owned allocation with explicit decoding and a finally cleanup on failure, or validate all tokens before allocating; retain the common reader rules and successful-output ownership.
findings.requiredVerification: Unknown first/middle/last UR pairs and full Bytewords must refuse with captured arrays zeroed. Keep CRC/metadata failures, known-answer success and caller-owned-output controls.

informationalReview.recommendation: Derive held from the captured normalized original. This requires executable host code and is recorded as robustness advice rather than a passive-input attack.

remediationAddendum.reproductionNote: residual-probes.mjs now passes four of its six checks. Its two transport checks hook Uint8Array.from only and require at least one array made through it; decodedBytes makes its array with new Uint8Array, so they report 0 allocations and 0 nonzero arrays and cannot pass. test/aud-016.test.ts captures every Uint8Array made (test/helpers/made-arrays.ts) and finds them all wiped for an unknown first, middle and last UR pair and an unknown last Byteword.
